subjects.authored_statement: Preserve verification_workspace, assessment authority, verification-matrix data, source identity, and coverage semantics.
The structural graph may consume and focus canonical verification results but must not derive or re-decide assessment state.
Do not classify absent structural mapping as absent authored or verification evidence.
Assessment, observation, association, graph-membership, collection, or acceptance semantics.
New evidence collection or LLM behavior.
Selecting an R/G/T/CC subject in the structural investigation surface shows its authored statement, canonical assessment, observations, and source in the same inspector.

Assessment and evidence detail is progressively disclosed by default, while the assessment state and any contradiction, missing evidence, incomplete collection, or other exceptional condition remain visible without expansion.
A subject without structural mapping remains available and shows its authored statement and non-structural evidence; absence from the graph must not remove it from review.
The page has one canonical R/G/T/CC investigation entry rather than a second repeated Verification section.
